paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, and I'm not going to pretend it isn't. A king, his three sons and his whole house die on a mountain, and Chronicles doesn't leave us guessing why. The writer says, "Saul died for his unfaithfulness to the LORD, because he did not keep the word of the LORD and even consulted a medium for guidance" (1 Chronicles 10:13). That's the lesson sitting right there in the open.

Look at what Saul did when he needed direction. He went around the LORD and went looking somewhere else, and verse 14 says he "failed to inquire of the LORD." I think that is the part to carry out of this passage. We all have moments when the LORD's answer feels slow, and the quicker option is sitting right there. Chronicles says plainly that the LORD is the one to ask (1 Chronicles 10:14).

And look at where the passage ends. The LORD "turned the kingdom over to David son of Jesse" (1 Chronicles 10:14). The kingdom doesn't fall into nobody's hands, because the LORD is still the One in charge of it. So here's your takeaway, baker: keep the LORD's word close, go to Him first, and trust that He's still holding everything, even on the heaviest days.
